The second round of talks will be held on Tuesday. They'll be mediated by Oman.
Araghchi will also meet with the head of the UN's nuclear agency as well as the Swiss foreign minister.
The first round of indirect talks took place in Oman last week.
Similar talks last year broke down after Israel launched air strikes on Iran.
Iran and the US restarted negotiations earlier this ⁠month.
They centre on a dispute which has lasted for decades over Tehran's nuclear programme.
There’s also an attempt to avert a new military confrontation. 

Al Jazeera’s Tohid Asadi has more from the Iranian capital, Tehran

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A US delegation will preside over talks on tensions with Iran, as well as the war in Ukraine on Tuesday, in Geneva. 
The news comes as day three of the Munich Security Conference is underway.
European leaders have been discussing ways to bolster defence and establish the continent as an autonomous global power.
The discussions come as concerns grow that Russia still poses a long-term threat to Europe. 

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has derided the Munich Security Conference as a “circus”, accusing European powers of “paralysis and irrelevance” in efforts to revive nuclear negotiations with the United States.
Iranian officials were not invited to the annual security meeting in the German city, and the top Iranian diplomat made the remarks in a post on X on Sunday, two days before Iranian and US officials are to hold talks in Geneva, Switzerland.

“Sad to see the usually serious Munich Security Conference turned into the ‘Munich Circus’ when it comes to Iran,” Araghchi wrote
title: Iran’s Araghchi slams European powers for ‘irrelevance’ in nuclear talks

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Israeli government has taken another step towards annexing the occupied West Bank.
It's opened land registration for the first time since 1967, when it first occupied the Palestinian territory.
The move means large tracts of Palestinian land could be confiscated and recorded as Israeli “state land”. 
Most Palestinian land is not formally registered because it is a long, complicated process that Israel stopped in 1967.
Registration of land establishes permanent ownership.
International law states that an occupying power cannot confiscate land in occupied territories.

Xavier Abu Eid, a political analyst based in Ramallah, said the “land registration” move by Israel is “packing annexation into some sort of bureaucratic move”.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Syria's army says it has taken control of a military base in the north of the country.
It's the latest stage in the implementation of a Washington-brokered ceasefire with the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) who partnered with the US to combat ISIL (ISIS).
Troops took over the al-Shaddadi base in coordination with the US, after it pulled its forces out of the facility.
It comes days after the Syrian military took over another base in al-Tanf, near borders with Iraq and Jordan, that was also used by the US military.
The takeover of these military bases is in line with a ceasefire agreed last month that aims to integrate the SDF into central Syrian institutions.
It ended weeks of tension and armed confrontations with advancing government troops.

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett has more from Aleppo, Syria.

Omer Ozkizilcik is a non-resident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council focusing on security, and a Turkish foreign policy specialist.

Israeli forces have bombed multiple locations across Gaza, killing at least eleven Palestinians.
The attacks are the latest violations of the ceasefire that came into effect four months ago.
Residential areas in Jabalia in the north of the Strip and Khan Younis in the south were hit. 
These areas fall within the so-called “yellow line”, the boundary separating the Israeli military from Palestinian residential areas.
Officials in Gaza say they've recorded more than 16 hundred violations of the ceasefire.
At least 590 people have been killed in attacks since October.

Al Jazeera’s Hind Khoudary has the latest from Gaza City, Palestine.

description:
African leaders at the African Union summit said the continent faces urgent challenges including insecurity, climate change and economic strain.
At the meeting in Addis Ababa, Antonio Guterres urged stronger global representation for Africa, noting many states were unrepresented when global institutions were formed.
He said fair governance is impossible without African voices shaping solutions.
Leaders stressed the need to resolve conflicts such as the war in Sudan.
Images of past leaders highlighted Africa’s push for influence in a shifting world order.
But young Africans criticised governments as out of touch with everyday realities.
Delegates pledged seriousness in tackling the continent’s pressing crises.

Al Jazeera’s Haru Mutasa reports from the summit in Addis Ababa.
